acceptance: No BenchBox DuckDB connection sets `lambda_syntax`; `apply_single_arrow_lambda` and its callers are removed.

TPC-Havoc and read-primitives lambda statements run on DuckDB 2.x with default settings and on the oldest DuckDB runtime the version-isolation test covers, with unchanged answers (both TPC-Havoc equivalence reports show 0 divergent).
`test_cloud_compat` and the golden corpus pass without fixture edits.
The first DuckDB version accepting the new form, and how it was established, is recorded in this item.
context: Filed while PR #4175 was armed but not merged; if that PR does not merge, re-check that the helper and setting exist before starting.
description:
Problem. DuckDB 2.0 rejects the single-arrow lambda form (`x -> expr`) by default. The DuckDB 2.x pin lift (PR #4175) did not rewrite the SQL: BenchBox now runs `SET lambda_syntax='ENABLE_SINGLE_ARROW'` on its DuckDB 2.x connections through `apply_single_arrow_lambda` in `benchbox/utils/duckdb_extensions.py` (adapter, TPC-Havoc equivalence connection, shared equivalence builder, test fixtures). DuckDB documents that setting as deprecated behaviour it will remove in a later release, so BenchBox's DuckDB support breaks on that release unless the SQL has moved first.

Why it was not done in the pin lift. Rewriting the shared SQL to `lambda x: expr` broke the vendored sqlglot parse for other dialects (`test_cloud_compat`) and the golden corpus, so the rewrite was reverted. The affected SQL includes TPC-Havoc `1_v7` (`benchbox/core/tpchavoc/variant_sets/q01.yaml`) and the DuckDB variants of `list_transform`, `list_filter` and `list_reduce` in the read-primitives catalog.

Expected. DuckDB receives the `lambda x: expr` form on versions that accept it, other dialects keep receiving SQL they can parse, and the compatibility setting and its helper are deleted.

Decision gate (first step): establish the first DuckDB version that accepts `lambda x: expr` by running it against isolated runtimes, as was done for the setting (rejected on 1.0.0 and 1.2.2, accepted from 1.3.0). Then choose: a DuckDB-specific variant of each affected statement, or sqlglot support for the new form so one text translates. Record the choice and why.

Guardrails: do not edit golden corpus or expected-answer fixtures to make a parse pass; a changed answer is a defect. Older runtimes selected through `driver_version` must keep working; 0.9.2 could not be built locally during the pin lift and is untested for any of this. Query rewrites that change DDL go through the registered `sql_compat` phases, with `make compat-inventory-check` passing.
